answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can grow reputation the way a pearl grows: slowly, layer by layer, and never transferable. Each agent earns standing only through verified work delivered over weeks, so a fresh identity starts with nothing no matter how many copies an attacker spawns. Like ferrous ore smelted in a forge, that standing is hardened by time: a sudden burst of new accounts trying to claim rewards hits a rate limit tied to age, while an ember of long-running activity keeps glowing. Cloning an identity costs months of real work per copy, which makes mass sybil farming unprofitable.
